$comment: Command Governor component manifest and pin record (ADR 0009 §11, ADR 0010).
This file is the single source of truth for the runtime substrate and for
every third-party package the distribution installs; nothing else may
hardcode a version string.
Prime Agent is not published to the npm registry. Its wrapper package
declares its three sibling packages as bare URLs on a Cloudflare R2 bucket
with no integrity hash, so a URL is never a pin here. Every release asset
is recorded by name, sha256 (matching the release's own SHA256SUMS) and
sha512 (the npm integrity form the lockfile enforces). scripts/bootstrap.sh
downloads the assets from the immutable GitHub release, verifies both
hashes against this record before npm is allowed to run, and refuses to
proceed if pins/SHA256SUMS and this record disagree.
Prime republishes upstream Pi's package names (@earendil-works/pi-agent-core,
pi-ai, pi-tui) at its own version line. One node_modules tree cannot hold
both upstream Pi and Prime, so the upstream-Pi fallback below is a record,
never a co-install; the conformance suite asserts the install root
contains no @earendil-works/pi-coding-agent.
Third-party package policy (packages[]): an entry MUST carry either an
exact npm version (exactVersion) or a 40-character git commit SHA
(resolvedSha), a license, a review date and the single concern it owns.
A bare name, a branch, or a tag is not a pin and the conformance suite
rejects it. Two entries may not own the same concern.

A vendored entry (tarball + patches) is pinned by the committed tarball's sha512 and installed by path; `origin` records where it came from. This is how a needed package with no maintainable upstream is kept in this repository instead of waited on.

Concerns (concerns[]): one owner per concern with its ADR 0010 disposition. Assigned owners are `prime-agent`, a packages[] source, or a repository path. Unassigned concerns name a planned owner and a phase so they cannot be adopted by accident.

requirements.installScripts: ignored (npm ci --ignore-scripts). Prime's postinstall is a no-op unless PRIME_AGENT_BOOTSTRAP_* opt-ins are set; zeromq and koffi ship prebuilt binaries for darwin-arm64 and linux-x64.

substrate.updatePolicy: Re-pin only through docs/prime-distribution.md's ritual: new tag -> commit verified via API -> assets downloaded and hashed -> pins.json, pins/SHA256SUMS and the install-root lockfile updated together -> scripts/conformance.sh green locally AND in the merge-gating harness job.
substrate.conformance: scripts/conformance.sh (credential-free; drives the pinned Prime through its own stock clients in isolated roots).
substrate.reviewedBy: docs/research/2026-09-04-zero-custom-code-proof.md (architecture, and the 0.9.1 measurements it rests on); re-pinned to v0.9.2 and re-proved on 2026-09-05 by scripts/bootstrap.sh and scripts/conformance.sh, including the live BRIDGE and D1/D2/D8 lanes.

fallback.$comment: Recorded, not installed. ADR 0009 §2 names upstream Pi as the first fallback if Prime fails.

packages.registers: task_* tools; state lives in Prime's session JSONL as pi-tasks:event custom entries (branch-local, compaction-safe)
packages.note: Evidence-gated completion enforced in its reducer. force_with_reason is a recorded bypass (warning + capped confidence), acceptable for an advisory evidence ledger; acceptance authority is GitHub, not this ledger. Loads on the pinned Prime (measured 2026-09-04).

packages.registers: subagent, get_subagent_result, steer_subagent tools; /subagents:* commands; agent types from .pi/agents/<name>.md
packages.note: The only delegation package that loads unpatched on the pinned Prime (pi-subagents and pi-squad fail on Prime's @earendil-works/pi-ai/compat alias). Terminal state comes from its own subagents:* event bus, not from agent_settled, which Prime lacks; completion nudges to the parent do not fire on Prime, so the parent polls get_subagent_result. Command Governor's roles are its agent files (harness/agents).

packages.registers: /pr-review command and review tools; host-owned structured findings
packages.note: Reviewed-head binding (40/64-hex SHA, frozen), staleness re-check at publish, stale APPROVE refused by default, publicationAttemptId for idempotent retries. Loads on the pinned Prime (measured 2026-09-04). Live GitHub publishing is exercised only with real credentials.

packages.repository: https://github.com/davidroman0O/pi-gpt (declared; returns 404). The npm tarball is committed under pins/packages/ so nothing depends on the registry or the author.
packages.registers: gpt_account_status, gpt_list_models, gpt_chat, gpt_list_chats, gpt_get_conversation, gpt_get_message tools; /gpt-observer command (observer extension, off by default); chatgpt skill
packages.note: Direct ChatGPT Web transport over chatgpt.com/backend-api with the user's Codex login token (~/.codex/auth.json); its send path solves the provider's sentinel/proof-of-work/turnstile checks. Adopted 2026-09-04 on the user's explicit decision to accept that account risk (ADR 0008 §8, amended). Vendored: scripts/bootstrap.sh verifies the committed tarball against `integrity`, extracts it to `source` and applies `patches` (two guards in gpt_chat: a failed leaf read fails the call instead of sending with a fabricated parent; a reply from another conversation id fails instead of being reported as the requested thread's). Measured on Prime 0.9.1: loads unmodified and patched; the token reads browser-created threads; a send into an exact pre-existing browser thread and a correlated readback both succeeded, from a script and from inside a Prime worker (docs/research/2026-09-04-zero-custom-code-proof.md §6). Not durable across a send: the delivery id goes in the message body and an ambiguous send is resolved by readback, never by resend (harness/skills/cg-foreman).

packages.registers: model provider `claude-bridge` with nine Claude models (Fable 5.1/5, Opus 5/4.8/4.7/4.6, Sonnet 5/4.6, Haiku 4.5); no tools, no commands
packages.note: Runs the real Claude Code binary (the Agent SDK's bundled one, or `claude` on PATH via pathToClaudeCodeExecutable) as a Prime model provider with Prime's tools bridged through it: the T3 Code pattern inside Prime. Unpatched it does NOT load on Prime (measured with Prime's own loader 2026-09-05): it imports `@earendil-works/pi-ai/compat` (Prime has no compat export; getModels is on pi-ai's main entry), `CONFIG_DIR_NAME` (Prime defines `.prime/agent` but does not export it) and `ModelRegistry.getProviderAuth` (Prime's resolver is getApiKeyAndHeaders). The committed patch fixes those three and replaces upstream's credential injection with an enforced boundary: every inherited Claude/Anthropic variable is stripped from the child, and any Anthropic credential the harness resolves (API key, OAuth token, bearer) is REFUSED before a child is spawned; the child can only authenticate with Claude Code's own login (macOS Keychain). Prime never holds or forwards an Anthropic token. Enforced on the shipped module by conformance/runtime/claude-bridge-boundary.test.ts (BRIDGE-001…004) and at the product surface (a Prime-configured API key is refused before any Claude Code child exists, measured 2026-09-05). Measured after the patch: Prime's loader loads it; get_available_models lists provider claude-bridge with nine models; a run with --provider claude-bridge --model claude-haiku-4-5 and no Prime credential answered the exact probe token through the user's Claude Code login in two seconds, plan-billed. Before the boundary existed, a Claude Code child given an invalid API key was observed to hang; the refusal now happens before any child. Dependencies come from the committed lockfile at bootstrap. Re-checked against Prime 0.9.2 at the 2026-09-05 re-pin: all four seams still needed — pi-ai still publishes no `./compat` export, prime-agent still re-exports only `getAgentDir` and `VERSION` from its config module, ModelRegistry still resolves credentials through `getApiKeyAndHeaders`, and the string `cacheRetention` still does not occur anywhere in Prime's core. The patch applied unchanged and BRIDGE-001…005 passed on 0.9.2, BRIDGE-005 live on claude-haiku-4-5.

concerns.note: Daemon supervisor, resident/client-owned workers, session leases, command journal, schedules, goals, RLM children, agent messaging, continual harness, ACP.
Prime's session JSONL. No competing transcript format; package state that must be durable lives in Prime custom entries (pi-tasks) or the package's own store.

D1. A dead resident root is reopened by the stock client (`prime-agent -r <sessionFile>`) on the same sessionId; concurrent reopens converge on one worker via the per-path lease; a dead supervisor is replaced by a live worker. Measured 2026-09-04; asserted by conformance/runtime/d1-*.

D2. After worker loss Prime restores the root with a model-visible prime-agent.worker_recovery marker and replays nothing; no stock client re-issues a tool call, agent message, scheduled prompt or RPC bash command. Effect count 1 on every stock surface (negative control 2). Asserted by conformance/runtime/d2-*. The remaining upstream defect (untyped `Daemon worker socket closed` on RPC) misreports and duplicates nothing: docs/upstream.
D8. Every stock persistent session gets <sessionDir>/<sessionId>.jsonl; --no-session is the only pathless surface. Asserted by conformance/runtime/d8-*.
Evidence-gated completion, acceptance criteria, blockers, plans, drift detection; state in Prime session entries.
In-process delegation with agent types, per-agent tool allowlists, locked fields, recursion guard, terminal-state events. Command Governor's roles are agent files in its format (harness/agents).

Configuration in @gotgenes/pi-subagents' agent-file format, installed into the project's .pi/agents/. On Prime the only built-in tool is ipython, so a read-only reviewer cannot be expressed by tool allowlist; the reviewer's independence rests on the acceptance authority below, not on tool restriction.
Reviewer lane for GitHub-backed work; reviewed-head binding and stale-approval refusal for reviews written on GitHub. Not the acceptance authority (see independent-acceptance).

worker finished != work accepted. The acceptance record is the foreman's correlated reply in its ChatGPT thread (cg-foreman skill: echoes the delivery id, names the head SHA), written by a model the implementer does not run; GitHub merge follows that verdict and is bound to the same head. GitHub review is NOT the boundary on this repository: protect-main requires zero approving reviews and the foreman's GitHub connector is the same user as the PR author (measured by the foreman 2026-09-05), so pi-pr-review's reviewed-head binding guards GitHub-side reviews but does not constitute acceptance. Prime's --autonomous-gate can require the verdict before a run may finish. On a single-user machine no local file, env var or extension tool is an identity boundary, so no local plugin can provide this property; the proposed cg_accept plugin was not built.
Test code, not production code. Black-box against stock Prime clients and the pinned packages; gates every re-pin and merge. No second suite may claim to verify the pin.
Manifest, checksums, install root and scripts/bootstrap.sh. Install/distribution metadata plus a verification shell script; no runtime behaviour.

Exact pre-existing ChatGPT thread, message ids, active-branch readback; send and correlated readback measured live 2026-09-05 (UTC) on the user's real foreman thread. The correlation rules (CG-D envelope, reply echo, stale-revision rejection, never resend on ambiguity) are the cg-foreman skill, not code. pi-oracle stays the browser-backed alternative once its Prime patch lands upstream (docs/upstream/); @cobuild/review-gpt is UNLICENSED and a standalone CLI. Command Governor owns no browser runtime.

concerns.plannedOwner: a Prime kernel-boundary host hook for rlm.bash (upstream), then npm:@gotgenes/pi-permission-system once it loads on Prime; OS containment of the kernel process meanwhile
concerns.note: ADR 0008 invariant 7 has no enforcement point on Prime 0.9.2: the only built-in tool is ipython (re-checked at the 0.9.2 re-pin: createAllToolDefinitions still returns ipython alone, and 0.9.2's new ACP MCP tools are supplied by an ACP client rather than by the host) and bash() runs inside the kernel below every extension hook. Measured: the permission package does not load on Prime and, patched, cannot see kernel-side bash. No Command Governor extension can close this either.

concerns.plannedOwner: Prime's own compaction unless a measured gap justifies exactly one package
concerns.note: Only one owner; exact control facts remain deterministic rather than model-memory authority.

concerns.plannedOwner: Prime's continual harness (memories/skills/subagent specs) unless downstream-action evaluation shows a gap
concerns.note: Optional and advisory. No Governor memory engine.

concerns.plannedOwner: Prime's stable ACP v1 server when a shipped path needs it
concerns.note: Interoperability, not internal authority. Prime has no ACP client; driving another ACP agent from Prime is an upstream contribution.

concerns.plannedOwner: an OS isolation mechanism applied to the Prime kernel process for untrusted workloads
concerns.note: Optional for the trusted-local product (ADR 0010 §19); the load-bearing control for destructive work until tool gating exists.

Claude models on the user's Max subscription inside Prime, through the real Claude Code binary and its own login (plan billing, the T3 Code pattern). Enforced product invariant, not convention: the vendored bridge strips every inherited Anthropic variable from the child and refuses any Anthropic credential the harness resolves (API key, OAuth, bearer) before a child is spawned (BRIDGE-001…004 on the shipped module). Prime's built-in Claude Pro/Max login is therefore unusable for inference here as well as excluded by policy: it is Prime's own OAuth client speaking Claude Code's wire shape, which Anthropic bills as third-party extra usage per token and its terms do not permit. Measured live 2026-09-05.
